fields.title: 1. Pricing — Primary Sources and Tier-1 Reporting
fields.md:
### 1-1. Apollo·Goldman Press Release (2026-11-20 11:02 EST, GlobeNewswire)

| Item | Content | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Title | 'Apollo and Goldman Sachs Announce Pricing of $44 Billion SpaceX GPU Financing' | [Apollo IR](https://ir.apollo.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/662/apollo-and-goldman-sachs-announce-pricing-of-44-billion) |
| Size | About $44 billion, senior and subordinated bonds · upsized due to oversubscription | Same as above |
| Purpose | Next-generation Nvidia Vera Rubin chips and related equipment — SpaceX's 'terrestrial compute buildout' | Same as above |
| Lease start | Begins when the GPUs and equipment are delivered, expected in the first half of 2027 | Same as above |
| Participants | Funds managed by Apollo and Goldman committed · anchors BlackRock, Goldman Sachs Asset Management, KKR advised accounts · Goldman sole structurer | Same as above |
| Not disclosed | Amounts, yields, ratings, maturities and closing date by tranche · SpaceX-side announcement | Same as above |

### 1-2. Pricing by Tranche (Reuters, 2026-11-20 — citing 1 person familiar with the sale)

| Tranche | Amount | Maturity | Yield | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A3 senior secured | $25.17 billion | 2033-04 | 8.259% | [Reuters(AOL)](https://www.aol.com/articles/apollo-goldman-lead-44-billion-174543000.html) |
| A2 senior secured | About $4.4 billion | 2031-04 | 7.66% | Same as above |
| B subordinated secured | $2.564 billion | 2033-04 | 8.36% | Same as above |
| Total (bonds) | About $32.1 billion | — | Weighted about 8.19% | Formula: 251.7 + 44 + 25.64 = 321.34 · (251.7×8.259 + 44×7.66 + 25.64×8.36) ÷ 321.34 = 8.185 |

- **Remaining about $12 billion**: by the formula 440 − 321 = 119. Reuters did not break it down by item. Bloomberg wrote that the overall financing includes 'senior secured loans and bank loans' (source: [Bloomberg(Yahoo)](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/spacex-sells-32-billion-ai-234112045.html), 2026-11-20).

### 1-3. Bloomberg (Smith·Barbuscia·Mutua, updated 11/20)

| Content | Source |
|---|---|
| Sold $32 billion of bonds on Thursday (11/19) · total financing exceeds $40 billion | [Bloomberg(Yahoo version)](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/spacex-sells-32-billion-ai-234112045.html) |
| About $26 billion was committed earlier, and the last roughly $6 billion (part of A3) was offered on Thursday | Same as above |
| Comparison: same-day average yield on US investment-grade corporate bonds 5.95% (Bloomberg index) · priced higher than SpaceX's June corporate bonds as well | Same as above |
| The package pays for about $47.3 billion of GPU equipment (Nvidia Rubin) · delivery expected to start in January | Same as above |
| SPV 'Saturn Funding Trust' (managed by an Apollo affiliate) buys the chips and leases them to SpaceX for about 5 years · rent payment obligation holds even with equipment failure or force majeure | Same as above |
| Off-balance-sheet structure · expected to help maintain investment grade · SpaceX and the arrangers did not respond to requests for comment | Same as above |

- **Contrast with the 11/05 record**: the '$47.3 billion Rubin chips' figure was recorded in the 11/05 round only through secondary reprints. It has now been confirmed by tier-1 reporting. However, it is still absent from the company's original text (source: `state.triggers_next_12m[T5].log_note`).

### 1-4. KBRA Preliminary Rating (2026-11-16, before pricing)

| Item | Content | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Rating | Preliminary A-, outlook stable | [KBRA release (Yahoo version)](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/kbra-assigns-preliminary-ratings-stable-115700547.html) |
| Scope | Senior A-2·A-3 about $27.2 billion · subordinated B about $2.4 billion | Same as above |
| Issuer | Newly formed bankruptcy-remote SPV · indirect wholly owned subsidiary of WHCO Intermediate Holdings LP — WHCO is an existing asset-backed lender unrelated to SpaceX | Same as above |
| Lease | WHCO → SpaceX, about 5 years · triple-net · 'hell-or-high-water' finance lease · quarterly rent fully amortizes the debt | Same as above |
| Basis | Lease obligation is 'absolute and unconditional' · strategic importance of the GPU equipment · economic incentive to keep the lease even in financial distress | Same as above |
| Downgrade sensitivity | Credit quality of the corporate anchor (SpaceX) — if leverage persistently exceeds 3.5x, large capital expenditure continues, or liquidity deteriorates | Same as above |

- **Preliminary → final size**: senior rose from a preliminary about $27.2 billion to about $29.6 billion at pricing (251.7 + 44 = 295.7, formula), and subordinated from about $2.4 billion to $2.564 billion. This is consistent in direction with Apollo's 'upsizing' (source: Table 1-2 · KBRA 11/16).

### 1-5. 'Chips on the ground' — Lender Demand (reported, unconfirmed)

- Motley Fool (11/20), citing the FT, wrote that lenders wanted a 'guarantee that the chips they financed would stay on the ground.' This is because chips sent into orbit cannot be recovered. It also wrote that it is unclear whether this went into the final documents as a binding provision. The FT original could not be opened (source: ⑥ [Motley Fool](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/11/20/spacex-just-raised-32-billion-for-ai-chips-lenders-want-elon-musk-to-keep-them-on-earth/), 2026-11-20).
- All the primary sources say is that the purpose is 'terrestrial compute buildout.' The KBRA release does not mention orbital use (source: [Apollo IR](https://ir.apollo.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/662/apollo-and-goldman-sachs-announce-pricing-of-44-billion) · [KBRA](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/kbra-assigns-preliminary-ratings-stable-115700547.html)).
